mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 2100 units signals increased consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence indices
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 55% of instances when HOUST > 2100, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 3.25% signals accommodative monetary policy, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 3.25% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market indicators and SPX performance
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of instances when trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a quarter signals reduced supply chain pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns after INDPRO declines are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) is a persistent driver of positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during positive GDP growth periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) growth exceeds 3% in a quarter, it signals tightening monetary policy and high inflation, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL growth > 3% in a quarter
evidence_refs: fact:historical monetary policy and inflation impacts on SPX
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 55% of instances when trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1% in two months signals labor market distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical labor market shocks and SPX performance
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE increases sharply, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) grow by less than 2% in a quarter and housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% in the same period, it signals weakening consumer demand, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth < 2% in a quarter and HOUST decline > 5% in a quarter
evidence_refs: fact:historical consumer demand indicators and SPX performance
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when trigger conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.
